extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language. The dataset contains SAT-style multi-choice problems collected from high-school textbooks and is designed for symbolic reasoning and interpretable geometry problem solving.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Geometry3K dataset was built by collecting geometry problems from two popular high-school textbooks via two online digital libraries, and groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem’s text, diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem was also annotated with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems from two high-school textbooks (grades 6-12) obtained through the McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline digital libraries, including problem text, geometry diagrams, four candidate choices, and correct answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. In order to evaluate the fine-grained performance of geometry solvers, we label each problem data with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) is referenced for human evaluation of problem solving, but no annotation platform is specified for dataset labeling.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance is reported for the collected problems: random guess accuracy is 25%, humans achieve 56.9% overall accuracy, and human experts achieve 90.9%.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had undergraduate degrees; additionally, dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering were asked to answer the problems for human expert evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MathPix OCR was used to recognize textual content in diagrams, and RetinaNet was used to extract diagram symbols and text regions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into train, validation, and test sets with a 0.7:0.1:0.2 ratio.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems were manually collected from textbooks and annotated with problem text, diagrams, candidate choices, correct answers, problem goals, geometry shapes, and dense formal language descriptions; annotators were filtered based on task requirements.
